title: Stock Market Today Live, September 18: Sensex, Nifty gain as lower oil prices and global cues offset IT, Tata stocks drag - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
GIFT Nifty futures were trading around 23,329.5 points, as of 8:30 a.m., ‌indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 ‌index, ⁠which closed at 23,270.60 on Thursday. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Equity benchmarks traded with marginal gains in the afternoon session on Friday, with lower oil prices and positive global market trends supporting sentiment despite weakness in IT companies and several Tata Group stocks.

The Nifty and Sensex are down 0.5% and 0.6%, respectively, so far this week, on course for a sixth consecutive weekly decline.

Among Nifty 50 stocks, UltraTech, IndiGo, Shriram Finance, HDFC Bank and Dr Reddy’s were the top gainers. TMPV, TCS, Coal India, Wipro and Infosys were among the biggest drags.

November Brent oil futures were at $103.85, down by 0.93 per cent, and October crude oil futures on WTI (West Texas Intermediate) were at $101.28, down by 0.62 per cent.

Deepak Chand Thakur, Managing Director & CEO, NPST, on the recent changes in UPI MDR on transactions above Rs. 2000

“The new framework for UPI marks a pivotal moment in India’s digital payments journey. Since its launch in 2016, UPI has transformed how India transacts, from street vendors to large enterprises, from metros to villages. The introduction of a sustainable MDR framework ensures that this remarkable public digital infrastructure can continue to grow, innovate, and serve every Indian for decades to come.

We commend the thoughtful design of this policy. By keeping 96% of merchant transactions and all person-to-person payments completely free, the framework protects the very foundation of UPI’s success – accessibility for common citizens and small merchants. The nominal 0.4% MDR on larger merchant transactions, which is significantly lower than credit card or debit card charges, creates a sustainable revenue model without burdening everyday users.

At NPST, we have been privileged to power the payment infrastructure for numerous banks and financial institutions over the past 13 years. We understand the complexity of building and maintaining systems that process billions of transactions securely and reliably. This policy acknowledges the real costs of operating such infrastructure and provides a path for continued investment in security, innovation, and expansion.

The framework also establishes a dedicated fund for promoting digital payments in Tier 3-6 cities, northeastern states, and among small merchants. This means the success of digital payments will directly fund greater financial inclusion across India.

NPST stands ready to support our bank and fintech partners in implementing this framework. Our teams are already working on solutions that will help the ecosystem transition smoothly by the October 15th deadline. We see this as an opportunity to deepen our commitment to India’s digital payments vision.

This policy change is the maturation of UPI from a government-supported initiative to self-sustaining financial market infrastructure. India has shown the world how to build inclusive digital public goods. Today, we are showing how to make them sustainable.”

The Wealth Company, part of Pantomath Group, has partnered with the International College of Financial Planning (ICOFP), promoted by Bajaj Capital Group, to launch the Applied Certification in Wealth and Financial Planning (ACWFP) for Mutual Fund Distributors (MFDs) across India. The programme aims to strengthen MFDs’ financial-planning knowledge and practical skills, including client communication, risk profiling, financial storytelling and responsible use of AI. Madhu Lunawat, Founder MD & CEO, The Wealth Company, said, “MFDs are among the closest financial partners of investors across India. As household wealth and financial participation grow, equipping them with stronger financial-planning knowledge and practical skills can meaningfully improve investor conversations and outcomes.” The initiative reflects a shared focus on building a more knowledgeable, skilled and investor-centric distribution ecosystem.

India has a “once in a generation” opportunity to move beyond semiconductor engineering and capture a larger share of the global value created through chip and system innovation, according to Vikram Meghal, SVP Engineering, Infosys.

Price Movement – Gold and silver clawed back some lost ground as softer oil prices and a weaker US dollar gave both metals room to breathe, even as traders kept one eye on the Middle East and the other on where global rate policy is headed next. The Bank of Japan pushed rates to a 31-year high and made clear it isn’t done tightening. The Bank of England, meanwhile, held steady on Thursday — but with a warning attached: rates could still move higher from here.

· Geopolitical Tensions – Supply-risk calculations are back on the table after Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis exchanged strikes on Thursday. In a notable diplomatic move, China has pressed Tehran to rein in the Houthis following their intensified military activity over the past week.
